usage: emit [-h] [--kind {observation,decision,intervention}] [--saw SAW]
            [--chose CHOSE] [--because BECAUSE] [--expected EXPECTED]
            [--id STEP] [--needs NEEDS]
            [statement ...]

Record one decision in this run's trace, as you make it.

positional arguments:
  statement             one line, if you prefer

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --kind {observation,decision,intervention}
                        observation: something you saw. decision: something
                        you chose. intervention: something you changed.
  --saw SAW             what you observed before choosing
  --chose CHOSE         the action you took
  --because BECAUSE     why, at the time
  --expected EXPECTED   what you expect to happen. Say it BEFORE you find out.
  --id STEP             name this step, at the moment you start it
  --needs NEEDS         earlier step ids this step depends on; comma-
                        separated, repeatable

instruction_source: Current user task message; these quotations are transcribed, not an independently signed seat contract.
instruction_quotes: RUN THE INCUMBENTS. Process Compose and Pueue are the SUBJECT of this unit, not its witnesses: start them, drive them through each of the six claims on the synthetic projects, and record what you observed.
The seat contract's 'you do not run the tests' means the lane's own witnesses (cargo test, the claims checker), which run after you; it does not mean 'execute nothing'.
Leave your work uncommitted. Committing is the operator's call, and a commit made here has to be undone before the work can be reviewed as a diff.
You do not run the tests, and you do not decide whether this passed. A witness you cannot reach runs afterwards.
